open_points.subject: K-02 function purity; M07 AdmissionVerdict and M23 NodeExecution
open_points.text: “no clock, no randomness” conflicts with “guards against depending on the time or on chance by accident; it is no guarantee against code written to get around it.”
open_points.question: Is absence of clock and randomness a product invariant whose breach makes a function execution invalid, or is it only a best-effort restriction under which deliberately circumventing code may produce a successful execution and be admitted?
options: Clock or randomness use is forbidden even when obtained by circumvention; a detected breach makes the execution a sandbox violation and prevents admission.
Only the standard-library entry points are withheld; code that circumvents that guard may still succeed, contribute passing trial evidence, and be admitted.
open_points.default_guess: Treat no clock and no randomness as the normative invariant, classify a detected breach as a sandbox violation, while acknowledging that an undetected breach may escape enforcement.

witness.initial: A contract has a nonempty trial corpus, and an implementation returns a schema-valid value derived from the current time through a route outside the guarded standard-library entry point.
events: An authoring agent submits the implementation.
The kernel runs its admission trials and the implementation obtains the current time through the circumvention.
The returned values satisfy the contract and the trial expectations happen to pass.
outcomes: Under the categorical purity rule, the executions are sandbox violations, the AdmissionVerdict is refused, and no Activation is created.
Under the new best-effort wording, the trial executions pass, the implementation is admitted and activated, and later runs may succeed with time-dependent outputs.
witness.observer: The authoring agent inspecting admission and activation, and callers or downstream nodes observing run outputs.
